concepts.learning_objective: Recognise that early timekeeping used natural events that repeat after definite intervals.
Describe how sundials, water clocks, hourglasses and candle clocks measured time.
Explain the working and limitations of ancient Indian water clocks, including the Ghatika-yantra.
Identify the mean and extreme positions of a pendulum and what counts as one oscillation.
Define and calculate the time period of a simple pendulum.
Analyse how the length and the bob's mass affect a pendulum's time period.

topics.title: Clocks and the SI unit of time

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that all clocks rely on a process repeating at equal intervals of time.
State the SI unit of time, convert between s, min and h, and write time units correctly.
Decide which object is faster by comparing distances covered in the same time.
Calculate speed as total distance divided by total time and state its units.
Convert speeds between m/s and km/h to compare motions.

topics.title: Relationship between speed, distance and time

concepts.learning_objective: Use the relations among speed, distance and time to find an unknown quantity.
Calculate average speed for journeys with changing speeds or stops.
Identify uniform linear motion as equal distances covered in equal intervals of time.
Recognise non-uniform linear motion in data and everyday examples.
State what a speedometer and an odometer measure in a vehicle.
